To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the percentage of the mammographic breast showing nodular or homogeneous density is inversely associated with age at mammogram and number of full-term pregnancy.
the percentage of breast showing homogeneous density and nodular density decreased with increasing age, and with increasing number of full-term pregnancy.

the extent of nodular densities on xeromamograms decreases with increasing age and increasing parity, and that the extent of both nodular and homogeneous density decreases with increasing age, increasing parity, increasing age at first full-term pregnancy, and increasing number of full-term breast biopsies or aspirations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relation of mammographic density to breast cancer risk.
the relation of breast density on mammography to the risk of breast cancer.
the relationship between mammographic features of breast tissue and breast cancer risk factors in asymptomatic women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the extent of mammographic density is related to age and parity but not to other breast cancer risk factors.
the mammographic appearance of the breast is related to age, the number of full-terms, menopausal status, and history of breast biopsy and/or aspiration.
the extent of nodular density in the breast is related to age and the extent of homogeneous density to both age and the number of fullterm pregnancies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mammographic appearance of the breast changes with age, parity, menopause, and history of breast biopsy.
there is a strong association of breast cancer with the presence of mammographically detected nodular densities, but that there is no association with the presence of homogeneous densities.
mammographic density is related to the risk factors for breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mammographic features of breast cancer are not related to breast cancer risk.
mammographic features are associated with breast cancer risk factors and that the relation differs for different features.
mammography has an important role to play in screening for breast cancer, and that it is a very effective screening tool.
